messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: sudden spike in 502/504 errors observed from gateway -> control-plane dependencies (auth/org-lookup). Error rate: 18% over last 3m. Paging on-call. runbook: controlplane-deps -> triage.

sam: I’m on it, grabbing context. Are we seeing a particular downstream (auth/org/billing) dominate?

maria: seeing both auth and org-lookup timeouts. Sampling traces show 504s when calling /orgs/lookup and 502s from auth token service. Sending flamegraphs in a sec.

devon: picking this up w/ infra. I see sudden TCP connection resets to auth cluster from gateway nodes. Could be connection pool exhaustion or routing change.

anya: adding telemetry: `curl "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(controlplane_5xx_total[1m])) by (service)"` returns auth=120, orglookup=90 in last minute.

jesse: customer impact: web request failures for hosted API and a handful of customer calls failing with 502s. No billing pipeline errors reported yet.

sam: ok, high-level plan: 1) stop new long-running queries hitting auth by throttling gateway -> backoff 2) re-route traffic to healthy auth replicas 3) roll forward a config revert if config change landed in last deploy.

maria: quick check: config-change webhook shows a config push 12m ago to controlplane-routing from infra-deploy pipeline. Reverting might help.

devon: I can toggle routing to prefer replica-a and replica-b (less loaded). Doing `kubectl patch svc controlplane-routing -p '{"spec":{"sessionAffinity":"None","selector":{"group":"replica-a"}}}'` in staging, then prod if green.

sam: wait on prod patch until we validate in canary. We need to minimize churn.

anya: logs (excerpt):
```
[auth-proxy] 2026-03-15T18:11:02Z ERROR upstream request failed: dial tcp 10.12.4.22:443: connect: connection refused
[org-lookup] 2026-03-15T18:11:05Z WARN timeout waiting for response after 30s
[gw] 2026-03-15T18:11:06Z 502 POST /v1/generate -> auth-service:502
```

maria: stack traces show connection pool at 100% on several gateway hosts. Could be too many idle connections or a leak. Setting `maxIdleConnsPerHost` to lower may help.

devon: ops-bot: spinning a temporary autoscale bump for auth replicas +1 for 10m to buy time.

ops-bot: Autoscale triggered: auth-deployment replicas increased from 3 -> 5 (ttl 10m).

jesse: note: customers A and B reported increased latency and edge 502s starting 18:10 UTC. CS looped in.

sam: Maria — can you run a targeted restart of the auth sidecars on the two hosts reporting `connection refused`? We suspect leaked sockets.

maria: doing rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-proxy -n controlplane --field-selector spec.nodeName=worker-17` (first host).

anya: also toggling gateway circuit-breaker to short-circuit to fallback token-verifier for requests older than 5s. Patch: `gateway-config circuit_breakers.auth.threshold=40` applying now.

devon: I’m also throttling non-critical background ops to reduce load: turning off org-lookup prefetch for 5m.

sam: good. After autoscale + restarts + circuit-breaker update, watch error rate. Maria, can you post metrics in 2m?

maria: posting current rollup: auth 5xx -> down to 9% (from 18%), org-lookup -> 10% (from 14%). Latency p95 improved 2s -> 600ms for auth.

jesse: CS update: some enterprise customers still seeing failures for large batched requests. Asking for temporary rate-limits on heavy-client endpoints.

sam: implement per-client backpressure on high-QPS tokens for 10m. Add a promo note to CS: "We’re mitigating an elevated rate of control-plane errors — applying temporary rate limits. We’ll update in 30m."

anya: config revert: I pulled the last routing commit and validated it introduced a change to a new pool selector. Rolling it back to previous commit now.

devon: rollbacks applied to routing repo (sha abc123 -> reverted). Gateway config reload initiated.

maria: after rollback + autoscale + restarts, error rate is down to 3% overall. Some spikes remain on a small subset of nodes.

sam: good progress. Next steps: 1) keep autoscale + restart for 10m 2) capture heap / socket metrics from affected hosts 3) postmortem owners: devon + maria + anya, due EOD tomorrow.

jesse: customer impact note captured: "Elevated 5xx affecting hosted API endpoints, limited to control-plane auth/org-lookup calls, mitigations applied: autoscale, routing rollback, targeted restarts, temporary rate-limits. No data loss reported."

devon: pulling tcpdump from worker-17 now, command:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/auth-failures.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host 10.12.4.22' &
```
Uploading to /var/tmp/incident/2435559999/pcap-1.pcap

anya: added temporary alert: `controlplane_5xx_rate > 5% for 3m` -> severity: critical -> send to #incidents. We'll suppress while oncall is acting.

maria: confirming health check endpoint for auth shows 200 on new replicas. Marking worker-17 as suspicious in the inventory.

sam: on-call handoff in 1h. Maria, please prepare a short summary for next oncall with links to logs, pcap, and the config diff.

maria: summary stub: "Routing config change (12m pre-incident) + connection pool exhaustion on gateway -> leakage on worker-17 led to spikes. Mitigations: scaled auth, restarted proxy sidecars, rolled back routing commit, applied circuit-breaker + per-client rate-limits."

jesse: CS notified customers A/B/C with the initial mitigation note. Will send follow-up after we have full timeline.

devon: following up on root cause: we saw one kube-proxy upgrade yesterday that changed ephemeral port handling on worker-17; correlating with start of degraded behavior. Opening an infra ticket.

sam: thanks everyone. Keep monitoring; if error rate creeps above 7% we re-open pager. For now, reduce noise and continue validation.

ops-bot: Incident incident-2435559999 created, severity: high, paging: completed, runbook: controlplane-deps-triage.

maria: last note before handoff: collected heapdump and pcap, uploaded logs to /var/tmp/incident/2435559999/, setting retention 30d. Handoff to night oncall in 55m.

sam: handing off to night oncall @devon + @anya for follow-up and postmortem. If anything regresses, page the SRE lead. :thumbsup:
